title: Assistant system-prompt variants must be changed together and guarded by wording tests
answers: How do I change Assistant prompt behavior safely?
Which prompt variants need updating when editing MLflow Assistant instructions?
Assistant prompt edit conflicts with another instruction
body:
Invariant: The Assistant has two system-prompt variants (the one in mlflow/assistant/providers/claude_code.py and the one in mlflow/assistant/providers/prompts.py). A behavior change must be applied to both, and a conflicting directive left in either one undoes the fix.
Why: In review, a new stop rule was contradicted by 'ALWAYS offer to complete tasks' in the Claude prompt, so the unwanted offers would still appear for documentation-backed answers.
Enforcement: tests/assistant/providers/test_prompts.py checks prompt wording. Negative assertions for banned phrasing run for both prompts in one shared loop, and positive wording assertions are kept variant-specific.
What breaks if skipped: One variant keeps producing the old behavior while tests pass, because the test only checks the phrasing that was changed.
applies: Any edit to Assistant system prompt text in mlflow/assistant/providers.
says: Assistant behavior changes work for one model provider but fail on another
The assistant still offers unwanted follow-ups when answering documentation questions
Keep assistant instructions and responses consistent across all supported model options
Fixed assistant conversation habits revert back depending on which provider is configured
search: Edits to Assistant system prompts in mlflow/assistant/providers must be applied simultaneously to both CLAUDE_SYSTEM_PROMPT in claude_code.py and prompts.py. Leaving conflicting instructions in either variant causes unintended behaviors to persist across provider configurations. Changes are enforced in tests/assistant/providers/test_prompts.py using a shared loop of negative assertions for banned phrases and variant-specific positive assertions. Applies to any modification of Assistant system prompt text across providers.
